lines.japanese: 今夜はいつもの現場仕事がなかった。
lines.english: There was none of my usual construction work tonight.

lines.japanese: 背広にメットのお偉いさんたちが視察に来るという。正規の手順を踏んでいない飛び込みバイトの俺は、ヒゲの監督から二、三日やすんでくれと申しつけられたのだ。
lines.english: Some bigwigs in suits and hard hats were coming to inspect the site. Since I was a walk-on hire who hadn't gone through the proper channels, the bearded foreman had ordered me to take two or three days off.

lines.japanese: とはいえ何もしないわけにはいかない。人間はアリやミツバチと同じ社会的動物なんだ。全体のために個々が何らかの役割を果たす義務がある。
lines.english: Still, I couldn't simply do nothing. Human beings were social animals, like ants and honeybees. Every individual had a duty to perform some role for the whole.

lines.japanese: よし。パルさんのところで、成田工務店への依頼がないか確認しに行ってみよう。
lines.english: All right. I'd go see Paru and find out whether anybody had work for Narita Construction.

lines.japanese: パルクレープは金土の夜でもないかぎり、そろそろ閉店のお時間だ。急ごう。俺はスポーツバッグを脇に担いで走った。
lines.english: Unless it was Friday or Saturday night, Paru Crêpes would be closing about now. I had to hurry. I tucked my sports bag under one arm and ran.

lines.japanese: 道中、どこか遠くからジェンベの音が聴こえてきた。
lines.english: On the way, I heard a djembe somewhere in the distance.

lines.japanese: 孤独なカラスは夜に鳴く。
lines.english: The lone crow cries at night.

lines.japanese: 「くっそ、間に合わなかった……」
lines.english: “Damn it. Too late...”

lines.japanese: ピンクのミニバンはどこにも見当たらなかった。
lines.english: The pink minivan was nowhere in sight.

lines.japanese: パルさんは撤収するとき、停車していた場所とその付近にいつもホーキをかけていくから、パルクレープ跡地は嫌味かと思うぐらい綺麗なもんだった。
lines.english: Whenever Paru packed up, she swept her parking spot and the ground around it. The patch where Paru Crêpes had stood was so spotless it felt almost like a reproach.

lines.japanese: 最近どうも上手く回らない。仕事も人間関係も。
lines.english: Nothing had been going right lately. Not work. Not people.

lines.japanese: 俺は個室ビデオ屋の壁に背中を預け、目を閉じて頭の中を空にしてみる。
lines.english: I leaned against the wall of a private-video shop, closed my eyes, and tried to empty my mind.

lines.japanese: しかし目を閉じた途端、その雑居ビルの細い階段からわいのわいのと騒がしい集団が下りてきて、おまけにそこから動かずわいのわいのと騒がしく語らいはじめた。
lines.english: The instant I closed my eyes, however, a rowdy crowd spilled down the mixed-use building's narrow stairs. Worse, they planted themselves there and kept right on making a racket.

lines.japanese: 三人、四人、五人……どんどん増えて、ゲーム屋から出てきた小学生みたいにはしゃいでる。うざい。超うざい。思考の妨げもいいところだ。
lines.english: Three, four, five... They kept multiplying, carrying on like grade-school kids just out of a game shop. Annoying. So goddamn annoying. I could hardly hear myself think.

lines.japanese: 「ぶはー！　もうマジしょっぱいわ～。やっぱねぇ、ゴメとデイトリが規制された時点で脱法系は終わってたンよ。その後もまあ、メチとかエースあたりはまだ使えたけど、今もう、そんなんすらアウトでしょう」
lines.english: “Phew! The scene is seriously pathetic now. Once Five-MeO and Daytripper got scheduled, that was it for legal highs. Methylone and Ace still worked for a while, but now even those are out, right?”

lines.japanese: しかも聞いてて趣のある話ならともかく、さっぱり意味不明の単語が頻出するから理解さえ出来ない。ＴＶゲームのアイテム談義か何かだろうか。いい歳して元気な男の子たちだ。
lines.english: If they'd at least been talking about something interesting, fine, but they kept throwing around words I didn't understand, so I couldn't follow a thing. Video-game items or something? Such energetic little boys for men their age.

lines.japanese: ＴＶゲームなんて俺には、脱衣麻雀と、メダルを賭ける競馬ゲームと、ウイングクエストのいっちゃん古いやつぐらいしか馴染みがない。そもそも今はあまり「ＴＶゲーム」なんて言い方しないんだろうか。
lines.english: As far as “TV games” went, about all I knew were strip mahjong, medal-betting horse-racing machines, and the very first *Wing Quest*. Did anyone even call them “TV games” anymore?

lines.japanese: 「ちゅーかもう合法でも違法でも、どのみちケミは終焉迎えてるンよねー。いま出回ってるバツなんて、多幸ナシでただアガるだけのシャブ玉ばっかよ。エルは供給自体が減ってるしさ、もうサイケ流行らんのよね」
lines.english: “Legal or illegal, chems are dead either way. All the E going around now is speed in a pill—gets you high without making you happy. Supply of L is drying up too. Psychedelics just aren't in anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「Ａｗ、ウェイトウェイト、落ちつけよオメエ。語りすぎで流石に引くわ。ロスの路地裏じゃねえんだからよ、ちったあ自重してくれよ」
lines.english: “Whoa, wait, wait. Settle down, man. That's way too much information. This isn't some back alley in L.A. Show a little restraint.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー、そんじゃさあ、アレってどーなんスか。あのほら、新型のアシッドとかいう？　最近日本でも流通始まったっつう噂もあんじゃないスか。名前なんつったっけ……エロイデス？　や、グロイデスか」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, what about that one? You know, the new acid or whatever? They say it’s started circulating in Japan lately too. What was it called... Lustorious? No, Gore-ious?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～、例の？　グロリアスでしょ、アレはねぇ～……」
lines.english: “Oh, that one? Glorious, right? See, the thing about that...”

lines.japanese: グロリアス？　なんだ、聞き覚えのある単語だな。
lines.english: Glorious? That rang a bell.

lines.japanese: ん？　つうか？　それ以前にこいつらの声、つうか喋り方、どっかで聞き覚えがあうような……？
lines.english: Huh? Wait. More importantly, their voices—or, well, the way they talked—felt kinda familiar...?
“Ugh.”

lines.japanese: しかし俺は目を開けて後悔した。
lines.english: I opened my eyes and immediately regretted it.
“Oh?”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ？」
lines.english: “Ooh?”

lines.japanese: 「おおおー！」
lines.english: “Oooooh!”

lines.japanese: こいつら……だったのかよ……。
lines.english: So... it was these guys...

lines.japanese: 俺はビデオ屋の壁にもたれたまま、うなだれる気力もなく濁った瞳で答えた。
lines.english: Still leaning against the video-shop wall, too drained even to hang my head, I answered with dead eyes.

lines.japanese: そして追い討ちをかけるように、同じ階段から下りてきたもう二人。
lines.english: Then, as if to finish me off, two more people came down the same staircase.
“Oh.”
“Oh.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは一瞬固まった。あの漫画喫茶の一件を忘れるほどまだ日は経ってない。
lines.english: For a moment, the three of us froze. It hadn’t been nearly long enough to forget what happened at the comic-book café.

lines.japanese: しかし忘れたように振るまうべきなのだと思った。俺だけじゃない、全員が思ったみたいだ。
lines.english: But I thought we ought to act as though we had. Apparently everyone else had the same idea.

lines.japanese: 「わ、わあ、隼人君じゃーん」
lines.english: “W-wow, look! It's Hayato!”

lines.japanese: 「お、おう、成田じゃーん」
lines.english: “H-hey, look! It's Narita!”

lines.japanese: 「や、やあ、成田隼人だぜ」
lines.english: “H-hello there. Hayato Narita, at your service.”

lines.japanese: 全員、役者の才能はないようだった。
lines.english: Apparently none of us had a future in acting.

lines.japanese: 「本当ですってＬＲさん、ネカフェのくせしてマジ美味いんすよ。もうチャーハンさえあれば、ご飯何杯でもいけンですよ」
lines.english: “I'm serious, LR. The place is an internet café, but the food's actually great. With fried rice like that, I could put away bowl after bowl of rice.”

lines.japanese: 「そう。で、シートも結構ふかふかなんだよ」
lines.english: “Right. And the seats are pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: 「あとシェフのまぐれサラダ、これキホン不味いんだけど、たまーに驚くほど美味しいときあってー」
lines.english: “And their Chef's Happy Accident Salad—it's usually awful, but every once in a while it comes out shockingly good.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう。でシートがまた、結構ふかふかなんだよ」
lines.english: “Exactly. And the seats, again, are pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: ある種の能天気さには、ときおり感心されられることがある。
lines.english: Sometimes I couldn't help admiring a certain kind of carefree airheadedness.

lines.japanese: 真似したいとは思わないが、千歳鷲介の処世術も理には適っているのかなあと思ったりする。
lines.english: I had no desire to imitate it, but perhaps Shusuke Chitose's way of moving through the world made a kind of sense after all.

lines.japanese: きょう俺が感心したのは、こいつらのしょーもないダジャレ下ネタだったり、しょーもない薬物講座だったり、しょーもないハイテンショントークだったりだ。
lines.english: What impressed me tonight was their idiotic dirty wordplay, their idiotic drug lecture, and their idiotic high-energy banter.

lines.japanese: 連中のしょーもないボケやツッコミに振りまわされているうち、いつの間にか場から妙なわだかまりが取っ払われていた──
lines.english: While their stupid jokes and comebacks kept me off balance, the awkward tension in the air somehow lifted—

lines.japanese: ──ような気がする。少なくとも表面上は。
lines.english: —or so it seemed. On the surface, at least.

lines.japanese: 「そんで、おまえら何してたの」
lines.english: “So what were you all doing?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、俺とＬＲでね、ちょいと若い子らを夜の社会科見学ツアーにね」
lines.english: “Oh, LR and I were taking the youngsters on a little nighttime field trip through society.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ」
lines.english: “What's that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「♪ケツの青いキッズたちに街の暗部をご紹介！　夜のギバラはまるでＳＨＯＷタイ、超退屈なら招待してやる、あんたもよければ一緒にどうだい」
lines.english: “♪ These green kids get a tour of the city’s dark side / Gibara after dark puts on one hell of a show / Bored out your mind? Come along for the ride / You too, if you’re game—what do you say? Let’s go!”

lines.japanese: 「いまは怪しげな喫煙具屋さんで、うっかり口に入れたら異次元的なところへブッ飛んじゃうサボテンとか見てきたとこなのよ～ん」
lines.english: We just came from this shady smoking-supplies shop, looking at these cacti that send you blasting off to another dimension if they accidentally end up in your mouth~!

lines.japanese: 「次は大人の銭湯に行って、うっかり中に入れたら楽園的なところへブッ飛んじゃうおねーさんとか見てくるとこなのよ～ん」
lines.english: Next we're heading to an adults-only bathhouse to look at ladies who'll send you blasting off to paradise if you accidentally put it inside them~!

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはない」
lines.english: “No, we’re not.”

lines.japanese: 「エエエェェーっ！　なんで！　フツー夜の社会科見学つったらそこは外せねッスよ！」
lines.english: “Whaaat?! Why not? You can’t have a nighttime field trip without that stop!”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿野郎おまえ、俺たちゃ分別ある大人だ、ガキが入っちゃいけねえ場所にガキを連れてくわけいくか」
lines.english: “You idiot. We’re responsible adults. We can’t take kids somewhere kids aren’t allowed.”

lines.japanese: 「エエッ！　だってチケドンさんいま、ヤバいサボテン売ってるとこに！」
lines.english: “What?! But Chikedon just took us to a place selling dangerous cacti!”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿野郎おまえ、ありゃただの観葉植物だ、人聞きの悪いこと言うんじゃないよ」
lines.english: “You idiot. Those were ordinary houseplants. Don’t say things that’ll give people the wrong idea.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、うっかり口に入っちゃったら幻覚的なものが見えちゃうけど、うっかり口に入っちゃった分には罪にも問われないしねフヒヒ」
lines.english: “Of course, if one happened to fall into your mouth, you might see a few hallucinations. But you can’t be prosecuted for something that fell into your mouth by accident. Heh heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「アンタその顔、うっかりする気まんまんじゃねースか！」
lines.english: “That face says you’re planning one hell of an accident!”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえら、もうちょっと付き合う大人は選んだ方がいいぞ」
lines.english: “...You two should be more selective about the adults you hang out with.”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょぶ、あくまで反面教師として参考にさせてもらってるから」
lines.english: “It's fine. We only use them as examples of what not to do.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、分かってねえな成田。ああ見えてあのひとらは、俺らなんかよりよっぽど沢山の知識持ってンだぜ。伊達に年食ってねえ、俺はいろんなことを教えてもらったよ」
lines.english: “Hah. You don’t get it, Narita. They may look like that, but they know way more than we do. They haven’t lived this long for nothing. They’ve taught me all kinds of things.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ。たとえば」
lines.english: “Really. Such as?”

lines.japanese: 「宴会で役に立つ爆笑一発芸とか」
lines.english: “Hilarious party tricks that come in handy at drinking parties.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ一個やってみて」
lines.english: “Then show me one.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ちょっと忘れちゃったわ」
lines.english: “Uh, I kind of forgot it.”

lines.japanese: なるほど。とても披露できないレベルなんだな。
lines.english: I see. So it was too awful to show anyone.

lines.japanese: じゃ、やっぱ役に立ってないじゃねーか。
lines.english: Then it wasn't useful after all, was it?

lines.japanese: 「おまえら、しょーもねえ暇潰ししてンなあ」
lines.english: You guys find the dumbest ways to kill time.

lines.japanese: 「ア～イ、まあ、ごもっともなんだけどお」
lines.english: “Aye, well, you've got us there.”

lines.japanese: レゲエ風があくびの出そうな顔でうなずく。ハゲやギャル男がしみじみ同意の表情を見せた。
lines.english: The guy in reggae gear nodded, looking bored enough to yawn. The bald guy and the flashy kid looked equally convinced.

lines.japanese: 「でもよお、実際ヒマなんだよなァ、太平の世の武士っつうのは」
lines.english: “But we really are bored. We're samurai in an age of peace.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁ～あ……どっかにこう、Ｒ－ウィングに代わる、次世代の悪モンでもいないもんスかねえ」
lines.english: “Yaaawn... Think there's some next-generation villain out there to take R-Wing's place?”

lines.japanese: 「大体さー、あの子ら降参すんの早過ぎなんよ。そんな簡単にあだ討ち諦めちゃっちゃー、愛しのハリューちゃんも浮かばれないよネ～」
lines.english: “That bunch surrendered way too fast. Give up on vengeance that easily and their beloved Haryu will never rest in peace.”

lines.japanese: やつらの会話に、今度は俺の知ってる単語が出てきた。Ｒ－ウィング。そしてハリュー・クロード。ガード下の派手な茶番劇が思いだされる。あの未明の事件は、まだほんの数日前のことだ。
lines.english: This time I heard words I knew in their conversation. R-Wing. Haryu Claude. The gaudy farce under the railway tracks came back to me. That predawn mess had only been a few days ago.

lines.japanese: 「へえ。なに、戦争終わったの。おまえら、あいつらに勝ったの」
lines.english: “Huh. What, the war's over? You beat them?”

lines.japanese: 俺はさして興味もなさそうに、さりげなく尋ねた。こいつらは（鳳が喋っていないかぎり）俺があのときあの場にいたことを知らないはずだ。
lines.english: I asked casually, doing my best to sound uninterested. Unless Otori had said something, none of them should have known I was there that night.

lines.japanese: 「勝ったつうか……ねえ？」
lines.english: “Beat them? I mean... You know?”

lines.japanese: 森里は仲間たちに微妙な同意を求めた。
lines.english: Morisato looked to his companions for hesitant agreement.

lines.japanese: 「６回表、５対１コールド勝ちっつー感じか？　これから面白くなるとこだったのに、すげえ消化不良で中途半端だよな」
lines.english: “Top of the sixth, five to one, game called. Just when it was getting interesting, too. Hell of an anticlimax—feels unfinished.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと」
lines.english: “What happened?”

lines.japanese: 「や・や・や、実はね！　こないだうちの皇帝がね！　Ｒ－ウィングの幹部をひとりフルボッコにしちゃったの、だはは！」
lines.english: “W-w-well, see! The other day our emperor beat one of R-Wing's officers to a pulp! Dahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら向こうさん、相当ブルっちゃったみたいでぇ。あっけなく白旗よ、はあ、つまんねえ」
lines.english: “And that must've scared the hell out of them. They waved the white flag just like that. God, how boring.”

lines.japanese: 鳳が倒した幹部──あいつだ、オウム頭の大司教だ。無邪気な戦争ごっこにいきなり本気の飛び道具を持ちだしたりして、仲間にすらドン引かれていた真性のアホだった。
lines.english: The officer Otori had defeated—the parrot-headed Archbishop. A certifiable idiot who had brought a real gun to an innocent little war game and appalled even his own allies.

lines.japanese: ところが柳木原フレイムバーズの鳳翔は、そのアホの凶弾さえ効かない、真性に輪をかけた超真性だった。
lines.english: Yet Kakeru Otori of the Yanagihara Flame Birds was so far beyond certifiable that even that idiot’s bullet had done nothing to him.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやー、強すぎるのも問題っすねえ、かかか」
lines.english: “Yeah, being too strong has its problems. Ka ka ka.”

lines.japanese: 「超真性……」
lines.english: “Certifiable squared...”

lines.japanese: こいつらはＲ－ウィングが恐れをなして降伏したなんて言ってるけど、やつらは恐れをなしたと言うより、敵も味方も頭がおかしいってことに気付いて、まともに相手をするのが馬鹿らしくなったんじゃないだろうか。
lines.english: They said R-Wing had surrendered out of fear. But perhaps they hadn't lost their nerve so much as realized that friend and foe alike were insane, and dealing seriously with either side was a waste of time.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、でも聞いた聞いた～？　そいつ、その、皇帝がボコにしたっつーオンナ男？　なんかねえ、病院から逃げだしちゃったんだって～、ぎゃははケッサク！」
lines.english: “Oh, but did you hear? That guy—the girly man the emperor beat down? Apparently he escaped from the hospital. Gahaha! What a riot!”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　なんだァおい、尿検でもされたらヤバいもん出てくるってかあ？　くくく」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that mean? Afraid a piss test'll turn up some bad shit? Kuku.”

lines.japanese: 「まあでも、もしあのオンナ男が口割っちゃったら、翔さんも面倒なことンなるわけでー。逆にトンズラこいてくれて、ありがたいっちゃーありがたい話なんすよねえ、かかか」
lines.english: “Still, if that girly guy spills, Kakeru's gonna have problems, right? So him taking off is kinda something to be grateful for, I guess. Kakaka.”

lines.japanese: 俺は舌先で口内炎に触れながら会話を聞いていた。
lines.english: I listened while touching the sore inside my mouth with the tip of my tongue.

lines.japanese: 大司教の脱走。それは笑い話で済ませていい問題なのか。そうなると、鳳翔は別の意味で面倒なことになるんじゃないのか。
lines.english: The Archbishop had escaped. Was that really something they could laugh off? Wouldn't that land Kakeru Otori in a different kind of trouble?

lines.japanese: だってそれは、気の触れたストーカーが傷と恨みを募らせたまま野放しになってるってことじゃないか。
lines.english: It meant an unhinged stalker was on the loose, nursing both wounds and a grudge.

lines.japanese: でも、まあ、どっちみち俺には関係が──
lines.english: But either way, it had nothing to do with—

lines.japanese: ──ある、のか？
lines.english: —or did it?

lines.japanese: あのとき俺は、ガード下の輝ききれない明かりの下に、瀕死の大司教を放置した。
lines.english: That night, beneath the lights that could never quite shine under the tracks, I had left the dying archbishop where he lay.

lines.japanese: あのとき俺がそうせず、一般的な義務と倫理に則って警察でも呼んでいれば良かったのか。それとも、くだらないことを考えないよう懇々と語って諭すべきだったのか。
lines.english: Should I have obeyed ordinary duty and ethics and called the police? Or should I have patiently talked him out of his ridiculous ideas?

lines.japanese: ……くそったれだ。巻きこまれただけの俺が、なんでこんな煮えきらない気分にならなきゃなんねえ。
lines.english: ...Goddamn it. I had only been dragged into this. Why the hell did I have to feel so conflicted about it?

lines.japanese: 「隼人君」
lines.english: “Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 暗い思考に没入していった俺を、くいと引きよせる手があった。うだうだ語りあうハゲたちをよそに、香田はさりげない小声で俺だけに言う。
lines.english: A hand gave me a small tug, drawing me out of those dark thoughts. While the bald guys rambled among themselves, Koda spoke in a casual murmur meant for me alone.

lines.japanese: 「ね、いまカズ君たちが話してんのって、佐久間君たちのことでしょ。こないだネカフェで調べたこととか言わなくていいの？」
lines.english: “Hey, Kazu and the others are talking about Sakuma's group, right? Shouldn't we tell them what we learned at the internet café?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いいよ。大したこと書いてなかったし無駄に巻きこまれたくねー」
lines.english: “Nah. There was nothing important on the site, and I don't wanna get dragged into this for no reason.”

lines.japanese: すでに若干巻きこまれていることは黙っておいた。
lines.english: I kept quiet about the fact that I had already been dragged in a little.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……じゃあ、べつにいいのかな？　あのサイトで、ちょっと気になる書き込みあったんだけど」
lines.english: “Hmm... Then maybe it doesn't matter? There was one post on that site that bothered me a little, though.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なにそれ」
lines.english: “Huh? What was it?”

lines.japanese: 「あのね、きのう家のパソコンで、もっかいだけあのサイト覗いてみたの。そしたら──」
lines.english: “Well, yesterday I checked the site one more time on my computer at home. And then—”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、隼人先輩！　あんたもこっち来て、俺らの武勇伝聞いてくれって！」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, Hayato! Get over here and listen to our tales of valor!”

lines.japanese: 「おー、聞いてる聞いてる。柳木原なんちゃらーズ、イェー」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah, I’m listening. The Yanagihara Whatchamacallits, hooray.”

lines.japanese: うぜえ。俺は邪魔な横槍を適当にあしらった。香田も同じように感じたんだろう。俺の手首を拾って小声で言う。
lines.english: Annoying. I brushed off the interruption. Koda must have felt the same. She caught my wrist and whispered.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとあっち行こ。自販機行くカンジで」
lines.english: “Let's go over there. Make it look like we're getting something from the vending machine.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはいいけど、いちいち手ぇ握んな」
lines.english: “Fine, but quit grabbing my hand every damn time.”

lines.japanese: 見てるんだよ、森里がちらちら。
lines.english: Morisato kept glancing over at us.

lines.japanese: 「は？　細かいなー。そんなこと今どーでもいいじゃん、ほら早くー」
lines.english: “Huh? You're so fussy. Who cares about that right now? Come on, hurry up.”

lines.japanese: 動かないでいたら、やつは俺の腕をまるまる体に抱きこんだ。なだらかだが硬い感触。森里の左眉がぴくりと跳ねた。
lines.english: When I refused to move, she wrapped my whole arm against her body. Something gently rounded but firm pressed against it. Morisato's left eyebrow twitched.

lines.japanese: 「だからベタベタ触ンなっつの。おまえには貞淑さが足りねえよ。こんなん大正時代だったら妊娠してんぞ」
lines.english: “I told you to stop pawing at me. You’re lacking in maidenly reserve. Back in the Taisho era, this would already have gotten you pregnant.”

lines.japanese: 俺は気持ち弱めにやつの手を振りほどいた。
lines.english: I shook her hand off with deliberately less force than usual.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　隼人君の好み、清純系？　ほー、じゃあアレか。こんなのか」
lines.english: “Oh? So you like the sweet-and-innocent type, Hayato? I see. Then how about this?”

lines.japanese: 「成田先輩！　あ、あのっ、お話があるので、よろしければ放課後、自動販売機前まで来てください！」
lines.english: “Narita! U-um, I have something I need to tell you. If you wouldn't mind, please meet me by the vending machines after school!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ話って。ハートで封した熊ちゃん便箋の手紙でも渡すのか。てめ言っとくけど、逆さに振ったとき山吹色のお菓子でも落っこってこないかぎり脈はねえからなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What do you have to tell me? Gonna hand me a letter on teddy-bear stationery sealed with a heart? I’m warning you: unless some ‘golden sweets’ fall out when I turn it upside down, you haven’t got a chance.”
“Here.”

lines.japanese: ちゅぽっ──いきなり香田が、それまで咥えていた棒付きキャンディを俺の口に突っこんだ。桃色の青春味。森里の右眉がぴくりと跳ねた。
lines.english: Pop—without warning, Koda thrust the lollipop she had been sucking into my mouth. The pink flavor of youth. Morisato’s right eyebrow twitched.

lines.japanese: 「まだ足りんかー？」
lines.english: “Need more?”

lines.japanese: 未開封の同じものがポケットから二つ三つと出てくる。
lines.english: She pulled two or three more of the same candy, still wrapped, from her pocket.

lines.japanese: フツーに美味いけど、そんな砂糖の固まりをホイホイ突っこまれたら虫歯になってしまう。俺は抵抗をやめて、十歩ほど離れた自販機に香田と連れだっていった。
lines.english: They tasted perfectly good, but if she kept shoving lumps of sugar into me, I was going to get cavities. I gave up resisting and went with Koda to a vending machine about ten paces away.

lines.japanese: 適当にジュースを買いながら、さっき途切れた会話を再開。
lines.english: We grabbed some random drinks and picked up the conversation where we'd left off.

lines.japanese: 「で、Ｒなんたらのサイトがなんだって」
lines.english: “So what about the R-whatever website?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いくつか新しい書き込みがあったんだけど、そん中に超ヘンなひとがいて」
lines.english: “There were a few new posts, and one of them was from somebody really weird.”

lines.japanese: 「Ｒなんたらの連中はもれなくヘンなひとだろ。今度はどんなだ。猿人か、地底人か、宇宙生命体か」
lines.english: “Every last member of R-whatever is weird. What was this one—an ape-man? A mole person? An alien life-form?”

lines.japanese: 「や、なんかそーゆーネタっぽい感じでもなくて、仲間内からもキモがられてる感じなの。もともとはＲ－ウィングの偉いひとだったみたいなんだけど、たしか名前、パトリなんとかって」
lines.english: “No, it didn't feel like that kind of joke. Even his own friends seemed creeped out by him. Apparently he used to be one of R-Wing's important people. His name was Patri-something, I think.”

lines.japanese: パトリアーク・ヨーゼフ。オウム頭の大司教か。
lines.english: Patriarch Josef. The parrot-headed archbishop.

lines.japanese: 「それなら俺も漫喫で見た。要はアレだろ、みんなレジスタンス起こそうぜーつって呼びかけてンだろ」
lines.english: “I saw that at the comic-book café. Basically he was calling on everybody to start a resistance, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうなんだけど、そのあと。隼人君はまだ見てないと思うんだけど、なんていうか……犯罪予告的な書き込みがあって」
lines.english: “Yeah, but there was more afterward. I don’t think you saw it. There was a post that was sort of... a threat to commit a crime.”

lines.japanese: 「犯罪予告」
lines.english: “A warning?”

lines.japanese: 香田の表情はおどけていなかった。こいつがマジで引くぐらいだから、その犯罪予告とやらには、相応の現実味があったんだろう。
lines.english: Koda wasn't joking now. If it had seriously unsettled even her, the threat must have sounded plausible enough.

lines.japanese: 「どんな内容なの」
lines.english: “What did it say?”

lines.japanese: 「えっと……」
掲示板上でのあいつらは、教祖たるロックバードの世界観に準じた文脈で語らう。ぶっちゃけ読みづらい。だから細かいところは覚えていない、と香田は前置きした。
lines.english: On the board, they spoke entirely through the worldview of Rockbird, their prophet. Frankly, it was hard to read. Koda began by warning me that she couldn't remember the details.

lines.japanese: 「どうもパトリのひと、フレイムバーズ全体っていうより、フレイムバーズの中の誰か特定のひとをピンポイントで恨んでるみたい」
lines.english: “It sounded like Patri wasn't holding a grudge against the Flame Birds as a whole. There was one specific person in the group he really hated.”

lines.japanese: 「そいつのせいで俺の人生台無しだーみたいなこと言ってて。それってフレイムバーズの一番上……翔さんのことだよね……？」
lines.english: “He kept saying that person had ruined his life. That has to mean the person at the top of the Flame Birds... Kakeru, right?”

lines.japanese: 「まァ……だろうなァ……」
lines.english: “Well... Probably...”

lines.japanese: 大司教を沈めたのもあいつだし。恨んでないはずがない。
lines.english: He was the one who had put the archbishop down. Of course the man hated him.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なるほど。そんで鳳の野郎をブッ殺すとか騒いでんのな」
lines.english: “Ah, I get it. So now he's ranting that he'll kill Otori.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、ちょっと違う。そうじゃなくて。翔さんじゃなくて、翔さんと関わりのある誰かをやっちゃおうみたいなこと言ってんの」
lines.english: “No, it's a little different. That isn't what he said. He wasn't talking about hurting Kakeru. He was talking about going after somebody connected to him.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんで──」
lines.english: “What? Why would—”

lines.japanese: いや、理由は簡単だ。フレイムバーズがＲ－ウィングの教祖に手を掛けたから。目には目を、歯には歯を、大事なひとには大事なひとを。
lines.english: No, the reason was simple. The Flame Birds had laid hands on R-Wing's prophet. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth—a loved one for a loved one.

lines.japanese: 聞けば実際やつは掲示板上でそう語っていたらしい。香田はそこが引っかかったという。
lines.english: Apparently, that was more or less what he'd written on the board. That was the part that bothered Koda.

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、翔さんの友達でしょ。ひょっとしたら目付けられちゃうんじゃないかな、大丈夫かな」
lines.english: “You're Kakeru's friend, aren't you, Hayato? What if he sets his sights on you? Are you going to be okay?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だろ。俺あいつの友達ンなった覚えねえし」
lines.english: “I'll be fine. I don't remember ever becoming that guy's friend.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でも傍から見ればフツーに友達だし」
lines.english: “But anyone looking at you would think you were friends.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなん言ったら、俺だけじゃなくて鳳と繋がりあるやつは──」
lines.english: “If you want to put it that way, it isn't just me. Everybody connected to Otori—”

lines.japanese: ──みんな危ない、おまえだって危ない。
lines.english: —they were all in danger. You were in danger too.

lines.japanese: 言いかけてやめた。いたずらに脅えさせてどうする。まだ確証もないことだ。
lines.english: I stopped before I said it. There was no point frightening her unnecessarily. None of this was certain yet.

lines.japanese: 「もし本当に誰かが狙われるんだとしたら、それは鳳にとっていちばん大事なやつだと思う」
lines.english: “If he really means to target someone, it'll probably be the person who matters most to Otori.”

lines.japanese: 話を逸らすために口を衝いて出た言葉だった。しかし的を得ていると思う。
lines.english: The words had slipped out only to steer the conversation elsewhere. Still, I thought they hit the mark.

lines.japanese: 「翔さんにとっていちばん大事な……？　って誰だろ、やっぱ隼人君？」
lines.english: “The person who matters most to Kakeru...? Who would that be? You, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ねーよ」
lines.english: “Not a chance.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ……彼女？　っているの？」
lines.english: “Then... a girlfriend? Does he have one?”
“Who knows...”

lines.japanese: セフレならいっぱいいそうだけど。
lines.english: He seemed like the sort to have plenty of friends with benefits.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いたとしても大事にはしてねえだろうなあ。あいつ病的に女を見下してるから」
lines.english: Even if he does, I doubt he treats her well. That guy looks down on women like it's a disease.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、友達でも恋人でもないとなると、あとなんだ……んー、家族？」
lines.english: “Hmm. If it isn't a friend or a girlfriend, what else is there...? Family?”

lines.japanese: 「家族か……」
lines.english: “Family...”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それもねーよな。詳しいこた聞いてねえけど、あいつちょくちょく父親から、はんぱねー額の金むしりとってるらしいじゃん。およそ親子仲良好とは思えねえ」
lines.english: Nah, that doesn't fit either. Don't know the details, but apparently he shakes his dad down for crazy money all the time. Doesn't exactly sound like one big happy family.

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもフレイムバーズの誰かが、翔さんシスコンだよなーって話してんのは聞いたことある」
lines.english: “Oh, but I did once hear one of the Flame Birds say Kakeru was obsessed with his sister.”
